scope: Internal reread found these issues before final scoring. Superseded candidate text is retained as drafting evidence, not accepted review.

before.speaker: A
before.text: For a wedding cake, we weigh the flour. Please put that mug down.

before.speaker: B
before.text: It's quicker. I've used three mugs already.

before.speaker: A
before.text: All right. Show me the mug, and I'll weigh one mugful.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I used three different mugs.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Of course. Please line them up by size. We're going to reconstruct breakfast before we can bake.

changes.4: Of course. Please fetch all three. Apparently we're measuring the crockery before we can measure the flour.

records.reason: Breakfast was an unrelated flourish; quantify the extra measuring work instead.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I've put my shoes beside yours for the interview. Very forward-thinking firm.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Mine are off because the heel broke.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Exactly. I prefer a preventative approach.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'll lend you my spare pair. The interviewer is coming.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Excellent. A change of shoes between reception and interview. I thought there might be a second stage.

changes.3: Then put yours back on. The interviewer is coming.
changes.4: Of course. Shoes off for reception, on for the interview. Very clear progression.

records.reason: A still has usable shoes. Offering spares creates a needless premise; B should request putting the original shoes back on.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Congratulations, Mayor Pudding Pants. Shall I sit with your mum?

before.speaker: B
before.text: Please don't use that nickname at my inauguration.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Right. Mayor Pudding. She'll know who I mean.

before.speaker: B
before.text: Just Martin. The microphones are already on.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Martin! Your mum's saved you a seat. Stop waving and come over.

changes.4: Martin! Come and sit by your mum. I'll move her handbag.

records.reason: Remove an invented waving action and a pre-saved seat. Invite Martin to sit beside his mother as a familiar child.

before.speaker: A
before.text: You thanked 'transport' in your award speech. I drove you to that audition.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I know. Let me buy you dinner to say thank you properly.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Somewhere with a good view of our award, I hope.

before.speaker: B
before.text: It stays in my office. I'll send you a photo.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Get my good side. I assume you've put it beside a picture of me.

changes.3: I'll put a photo of you beside it. Will that do?
changes.4: Use the one of us in the car. People should see how the award got there.

records.reason: The assumed portrait beside the trophy was strained. B should explicitly offer a photo; A dictates which photo credits the ride.

before.speaker: A
before.text: I've packed your lunch and labelled your umbrella. Again.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'm working from home today. You can leave it to me.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Then I'll put your lunch in the fridge. Apparently I need your work calendar too.

before.speaker: B
before.text: I'll share it with you. Tomorrow says lunch out.

before.speaker: A
before.text: Already booked you a table. Now I have to ring and check they have somewhere for your umbrella.

changes.4: I'll book you a table, then. Now I have to ring and check they have somewhere for your umbrella.

records.reason: Already booked is unsupported by A only now learning tomorrow lunch is out. Change this to an immediate unsolicited plan.
